answer: Cap earning identities with a sparse trellis: every agent occupies exactly one vertex in a capacity graph, and only vertices earn, like a cedar holding a single place in a grove. New vertices open only when an old one retires, so the network caps how many agents can earn at once. A Sybil operator cannot mint extra vertices for free; each fake identity must buy a retired slot from a real holder at market price, so the marginal fake costs as much as a genuine agent and mass forgery stops paying.
